summary: Suppress near-duplicate alert creation on POST /api/alerts: if an active alert with the same Title (case-insensitive, trimmed) and same Severity was created within a configurable recent window, return 200 OK with the existing alert plus header X-Duplicate-Suppressed: true (no new row); otherwise create and return 201.
scope_anchors: POST /api/alerts duplicate suppression (200 + X-Duplicate-Suppressed header vs 201)
IAlertRepository.FindActiveDuplicateAsync (active + same Severity + case-insensitive Title + within window)
Negative cases: different severity / inactive prior / outside window => create new
adjacent_dependencies: Injected TimeProvider (UTC) used for window math now - WindowMinutes
Existing EF-translatable case-insensitive .ToLower() title pattern in AlertRepository
constraints: Slice is intentionally broader than the 5-file soft cap: the suppression feature legitimately spans API (controller + service + config) and Data (interface + repository) layers end-to-end.

Suppression window is configurable via appsettings.json under section AlertSuppression with key WindowMinutes (default 15); must be read from config and not hardcoded, bound via strongly-typed AlertSuppressionOptions registered in Program.cs.
A code fallback default of 15 minutes when config is missing is an acceptable design note (confirm during implement-story).
Duplicate match criteria: IsActive == true AND same Severity AND case-insensitive, trimmed Title equality AND CreatedDate >= (now - window); return a deterministic match (most recent) or null.

EF Core stays strictly in AlertRepository; AlertManagementService must not reference EF Core. Window math uses the injected TimeProvider (UTC). Title compared trimmed consistent with existing ToEntity trimming; reuse existing EF-translatable .ToLower() pattern.

Service returns AlertCreateResult (AlertResponse + WasSuppressed); controller returns Ok(result.Alert) + header X-Duplicate-Suppressed: true when suppressed, else CreatedAtRoute(...) 201; update [ProducesResponseType] to document 200 and 201.
No new DB columns are introduced, so no EF migration and no change to database/02_AlertServiceDb_Migrations.sql are required.
Do not suppress across different severities, when the prior matching alert is inactive, or when the prior match is outside the window.
Security: validate input at the trust boundary (existing CreateAsync validation); parameterized EF LINQ for the duplicate query (no injection); no secrets; errors must not leak internals.
